evidence: Etymonline: "Old English bringan 'to bear, convey, take along in coming; bring forth, produce, present, offer'... There are no exact cognates outside Germanic, but it appears to be from PIE *bhrengk-..., which, according to Watkins, is based on root *bher- (1) 'to carry,'... but Boutkan writes, 'We are probably dealing with a Germanic/Celtic substratum word.'"
Etymonline: "The tendency to conjugate this as a strong verb on the model of sing, drink, etc., is ancient"
bring.mechanism_sentence: bring 的画面是『随身带过来』：人来，东西跟着来。它可能与 bear（承载）同出一根，也可能只是日耳曼—凯尔特的底层土词——两位学者（Watkins、Boutkan）至今没有吵出结果。

semantic_path.how: 核心义纹丝未动，两千年都是『把某物随人带到』。词库的过去式 brought 是它弱变化的老式（方言里另有学强动词的 brung，是它古来就有的摇摆）。

evidence: Etymonline: "from PIE root *ed- 'to eat.' The transferred sense of 'corrode, wear away, consume, waste' is from 1550s. The meaning 'to preoccupy, engross' (as in what's eating you?) is recorded by 1893."
eat.mechanism_sentence: eat 出自印欧语最不可缺的老根 *ed-（拉丁语 edere 是亲戚）：它本分了一千多年，只在近代学会了『吃』别的东西——酸吃金属，烦恼吃人。

semantic_path.how: 本义稳定；1550年代添转指义『腐蚀、耗损』，1893年又能指心事缠人。词库的过去式 ate 是强动词的老变格。

evidence: Etymonline: "It became yiven in Middle English, but changed to guttural 'g' by influence of Old Norse gefa 'to give,' Old Danish givæ."
give.mechanism_sentence: give 的本义千年没动，倒是发音改过籍：中古英语它读作 yiven，受了维京语 gefa 的影响，开头才换上了硬 g。英语的『给』，是托北欧人的口音定的型。

semantic_path.how: 词义稳定；1570年代添『屈服、让步』一头（give 本作名词即『弹性』）。它的老根 *ghabh- 本是双向的『给与取』——给出与收下，同根而生。

evidence: Etymonline: "Old English locian 'use the eyes for seeing, gaze, look, behold, spy'... In Old English, usually with on; the use of at began 14c.... meaning 'to have a certain appearance, express or manifest by looks' is from c. 1400."
Wiktionary: "Further origin unknown, no certain cognates outside Germanic."
look.mechanism_sentence: look 是西日耳曼语的土词，来历至今查不清。它管的是『主动地看』，与 see『看见』分工：词库的 look at 直到14世纪才定型；『看起来像』一义（约1400年），是从『被看到的样子』转到事物自己头上的。

semantic_path.how: 约1300年添『搜寻』义（look for 的祖型）；约1400年添『朝向』（房屋朝南）与『显得』两义。词库的『看（look at）』在本行。

evidence: Etymonline: "Old English open 'not closed down, raised up' (of gates, eyelids, etc.), also 'exposed, evident, well-known, public'... from Proto-Germanic *upana-, literally 'put or set up'... from PIE root *upo 'under,' also 'up from under,' hence also 'over.' Related to up"
牛津: "related to Dutch open and German offen, from the root of the adverb up"
open.mechanism_sentence: open 和 up 是至亲：它字面是『被向上托起、掀起的』——盖子掀开、眼皮抬起、门扇推上，就是 open。这个『开』从古英语起就两头管：管实物，也管人的坦率（心里不关着门）。

semantic_path.how: 义域逐个亮相：约1200年『无遮拦的（空间）』、14世纪早期『坦率』、1824年商店『营业中』——全是『没有关着』的投影。动词 open（打开）是形容词的老搭档同源词。词库的『打开/开着的』双义俱全。

changes: 第二站 how 改为有内容的编年说明（原为套话），补1300年『掷投』与14世纪诸引申的编年
evidence: Etymonline: "from late Old English *putian, 'to thrust, push, shove' (someone or something; a sense now obsolete), also 'to move a thing physically so as to place it in some situation'"

Etymonline: "From c. 1300 as 'to hurl, cast, propel'... From mid-14c. in the figurative sense of 'bring (someone) into some specified state or condition'... late 14c. as 'make a declaration, express in speech or writing'"
牛津: "Old English (recorded only in the verbal noun putung), of unknown origin"
put.mechanism_sentence: put 起家是『一把推过去』：推到位，东西便『放』在了那儿。几百年里它的手劲越来越轻——从猛推、掷投，到轻轻地『放下』，还顺手管了『表达』：把话『放』出来，也是一种 put。

semantic_path.how: 词义从动作滑向结果：推的终点就是『放好』，日常核心义于是定格在『放置』；引申支线有『使处于某状态』（put to death)、『陈述』（put it this way）等。词库的『放』在主线上，过去式与原形同形（put-put-put）是它弱变化简化后的样子。

changes: 路径由4站重排为2站：原第一站取印欧词根 *sekʷ- 的注义作路径站、第二三站 how 均为套话式，按编年并为古英语首站（seon 义域本来眼脑并兼）

evidence: Etymonline: "from Old English seon... 'be or become aware of by means of the eye; look, behold;' also 'perceive mentally, understand'... This is reconstructed to be from PIE root *sekw- (2) 'to see.' That PIE root often was said to be probably identical with *sekw- (1) 'to follow'... but OED finds this 'involves a hypothetical sense-development which it is not easy to accept with confidence'"
Etymonline 引 OED: "mental perceptions are in many (perh. in all) languages referred to in visual terms... English see has been used in many of these senses since early Middle English"
see.mechanism_sentence: see 在古英语里就眼脑双管：看见与懂得，是同一个词。它的老根或许与『跟随』同源——『用眼睛追着看』（此说 OED 存疑）；不管老根如何，『看见即明白』（I see，我懂了）这层用法，英语从中古一直用到今天。

semantic_path.how: 约1200年心智支线成套（预见、想象中看见、领会证明的分量）；约1300年添『确保、办妥』（see to it)。词库的『看见』在本行，过去式 saw 是强动词老变格的遗存。

evidence: Etymonline: "c. 1300, trien, 'to separate (one thing) from another or others, set apart, distinguish;' especially 'separate the good or desired part from the rest,' from Anglo-French trier (13c.), Old French trier 'to pick out, cull' (12c.), from Gallo-Roman *triare, a word of unknown origin."

Etymonline: "It is attested by mid-14c. in the chiefly legal sense of 'examine and determine judicially'... and by 1530s as 'subject (patience, endurance, etc.) to severe strain.' By early 14c. as 'attempt.'"
try.mechanism_sentence: try 的老本行是『筛』：把好的从一堆里细查着挑出来。它先上了法庭（审案就是细查后定夺），再下了生活（验一验人或物的成色）——『试着去做』这一义，是从『先验过再说』滑过来的。

semantic_path.period: 古法语时期（约1300年进入英语）

semantic_path.how: 从『细查后挑出』长出『审查、评定』：14世纪中叶，它在法庭上是『审理』，在生活里是『放到考验中考一考』（词义由分拣转为检验）。
『试图、尝试』在14世纪早期已出现，后来后来居上成了门面义（词义重心转移）。词库的『尝试』在这一站；法庭上的 try（审案）是上一站的活化石。
